clue.text: Chafing from one undergarment is no trouble

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up and disturb it, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: a and one both mean a single thing
a bra is a woman's undergarment
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone insists that the rubbing from their underwear causes them no bother.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasion is the scraping or rubbing away of skin, which is what chafing does.

clue.text: A detail in the English module, originally

indicators.note: originally points to the origin of each word, its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A student notes a small point covered in their English course.
explanation.walkthrough: The word in looks like it belongs to the surface sentence, but it supplies the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single particular in a list or account, synonymous with a detail.

clue.text: A mode of transport America provided for a mythical flyer

blocks.note: a means one, written as the Roman numeral
a car is a means of getting about
the usual abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: The United States supplies a vehicle for a legendary airman.
explanation.walkthrough: Turning A into I needs two steps: a is one, and one is the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew on wings of wax and feathers made by his father Daedalus, falling when the sun melted them.

clue.text: Smart illumination for swimmer

blocks.note: to smart is to sting with pain
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Someone recommends clever lighting for a person in the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: Smart reads as an adjective meaning stylish, but it is the verb meaning to hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat fish, a creature that lives by swimming, so it is a swimmer by example.

clue.text: At home, fit but not qualified

blocks.note: someone at home is in
fit in the sense of suitable or entitled

explanation.surface: A would-be athlete trains at home and is in shape, yet lacks the credentials.
explanation.walkthrough: Fit suggests physical health; here it means suitable for selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineligible describes someone lacking the conditions needed to be chosen or to take part.

clue.text: Noel got up, going round the vessel for punishment

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading the word from bottom to top
going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: the name taken as written
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A man named Noel rose and walked around the ship as a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel read upwards becomes LEON, which is split open around SS to give LESSON.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson can be a salutary experience that teaches by punishing, as in 'let that be a lesson to you'.

clue.text: Criminal stole cab but met a problem

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted out of place

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook took a taxi but ran into difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle is something that stands in the way, a hindrance or difficulty.

clue.text: Tribute to you, it's said, over record year

indicators.note: it's said tells us to go by how the word is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: these two letters pronounced together say the word you
a log is a written record, as on a ship
the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Someone is praised for a year of record-breaking achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a speech or piece of writing in praise of someone, often at a funeral.

clue.text: Bid for a boat

blocks.note: first meaning: a formal offer to supply goods or do work at a price
second meaning: a small vessel that ferries people or supplies to a larger ship

explanation.surface: An offer made to buy a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is both a formal offer of a price and a small supply boat attending a ship.

clue.text: Flickering lamp on hand

indicators.note: flickering light is unsteady and jumping about, so the letters jump into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A wavering lamp is held in someone's hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm is the inner surface of the hand, a part standing for the whole.

clue.text: Stubborn, will give way comparatively little

blocks.note: to relent is to yield or soften
less is the comparative of little

explanation.surface: A stubborn person will only yield a fraction.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pits stubbornness against giving way, yet giving way is a piece of the opposite word.
explanation.definitionFit: Relentless means unyielding and persistent, never easing off, much like obstinate.

clue.text: At noon on motorway coming back, vehicle was in cloud

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the motorway is read backwards

blocks.note: N is short for noon
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, with 1 written as I
a bus is a road vehicle

explanation.surface: Driving home along the motorway at midday, the coach was in fog.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London to Leeds motorway; crosswords write it MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimbus is a rain cloud, the dark grey kind that brings steady rain.

clue.text: It's nonsense to bash ladder at random

indicators.note: at random means in no particular order, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Hitting a ladder aimlessly makes no sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is senseless talk or writing, a colourful word for rubbish or drivel.

clue.text: Keeping a car off the street makes Georgia extremely angry

definitions.text: Keeping a car off the street

blocks.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
raging means furious

explanation.surface: Parking restrictions drive a woman named Georgia into a fury.
explanation.walkthrough: Extremely looks like an instruction to take outer letters, but here it just intensifies angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Garaging a car is putting it in a garage, a shelter that keeps it off the road.

clue.text: Sailor from Tyneside's little boy

blocks.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, abbreviated NE
L is short for little
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A seaman comes from a young lad in Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area round Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson was Britain's most famous admiral, killed at Trafalgar in 1805.

clue.text: Newspaper reporter

blocks.note: first meaning: a British Sunday paper, the oldest in the world
second meaning: one who watches and reports what they see

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a journalist on a paper; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Observer is a long-running British Sunday title, and an observer is a witness who notes and relays events.

clue.text: Reported sign of musical instrument

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so what counts is the spoken sound

blocks.note: a cymbal is a brass percussion plate, pronounced like the answer

explanation.surface: Someone notes a mention of some indication of a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A symbol is a mark or figure that stands for something else, as a sign does.

clue.text: Student with service on continent

blocks.note: L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
with and and both add one thing to another
Mass is the Catholic church service

explanation.surface: A student goes to church while travelling in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain learner drivers display a red L plate, which is why L stands for student.
explanation.definitionFit: A continent is a large continuous expanse of land, which is what a landmass is.

clue.text: Bird and animal's age

blocks.note: a pig is a farm animal
an eon is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: Someone asks a vet about a bird and how old a beast is.
explanation.definitionFit: The pigeon is a common plump bird of the dove family, familiar in city squares.

clue.text: Wears kit designed to enjoy sport on a lake

indicators.note: something designed is planned and put together afresh, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone puts on specially made gear for a day on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Designed seems to describe the kit, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To waterski is to be towed behind a motorboat on skis, a pastime on lakes and the sea.

clue.text: Goodbyes ending with a kiss

blocks.note: a farewell marks the end of a meeting
X is the kiss written at the foot of a letter

explanation.surface: Farewells finish off with a peck on the cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: ADIEUX is the French plural of adieu, used in English too.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a borrowed French word of parting, so its plural means farewells.

clue.text: Getting old silver quarter for a mixed gin

indicators.note: a mixed drink has its parts stirred together, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
east is one of the four compass quarters
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly drinker pays twenty-five silver pence for a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: A quarter in crosswords is often a compass point: N, S, E or W.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageing is the process of growing older, so the participle matches getting old.

clue.text: The way that groups reveal reserves

blocks.note: as means in the way that, as in 'do as I say'
sets are collections or groups

explanation.surface: How organisations behave shows what they hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are resources held in hand, like savings or stocks kept in reserve.

clue.text: More primitive Scottish loch in uncultivated region

blocks.note: wilder is the comparative of wild, untamed
Loch Ness is the Scottish lake of monster fame

explanation.surface: A rugged Highland lake sits in untamed country.
explanation.walkthrough: In seems to ask for one piece inside another, but here it only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wilderness is wild land left untouched by farming or settlement.

clue.text: Members' arsenal

blocks.note: first meaning: limbs of the body
second meaning: weapons

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the members of a club, perhaps Arsenal football club; members here are limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the upper limbs and weaponry, the stock of an arsenal.

clue.text: Wary, perhaps, when things go wrong

definitions.note: describes a state; the answer is an adjective or adverb meaning amiss

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word could be arranged otherwise, so its letters are shuffled

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone becomes cautious once trouble starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans that go awry turn out badly, so awry means amiss or off course.

clue.text: Persevere to make us pure, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters might be put another way, signalling a rearrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A preacher urges steadfastness as the path to holiness.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue a goal is to keep at it, continuing steadily, which is what persevering means.

clue.text: One living in the altogether simple style

definitions.text: One living in the altogether simple style

blocks.clueFragment: One living in the altogether simple style
blocks.note: surface reading: someone who lives an entirely plain, unfussy life
setter's reading: in the altogether is British slang for stark naked, so this is someone who lives unclothed

explanation.walkthrough: Altogether looks like an adverb meaning wholly; read with the, it is a noun for nakedness.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who practises nudism lives without clothes, the purest simple style of all.
